# AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU prices about 15% from October 7

Reserving B300 GPUs through EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now costs $16.146 per GPU-hour, up from $14.04. On-Demand and Savings Plans prices did not change.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

AWS raised the prices of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML on October 7, 2026. Capacity Blocks let you reserve GPU instances for a set period and pay for them up front. A notice on AWS’s pricing page gave the new hourly rates per accelerator, about 15% above the old ones. It also said On-Demand and Savings Plans prices stay the same.

## Old and new rates

Per GPU-hour in US regions. The large sizes (48xlarge and 24xlarge) have 8 GPUs each, so a full instance costs 8 times these rates.

| Instance | GPU | Before | From October 7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.04 | $16.146 |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 |
| P5e | H200 | $5.97 | $6.866 |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191 | $5.970 |
| P4de | A100 | $2.214 | $2.546 |
| P4d | A100 | $1.475 | $1.696 |

A full p6-b300.48xlarge now costs $129.168 an hour, up from $112.32. Outside the US the rise was bigger for some instances: P5 used to cost $4.72 per GPU-hour there and now costs $5.970, the same as in the US. In AWS GovCloud, P6-B300 is $16.819 and P6-B200 $14.801.

## The second rise since July

AWS also raised these prices in July. Before that change, the page listed P6-B300 at $11.70 and P5 at $4.326 per GPU-hour in US regions. Since June, both are up about 38%.

## How you are charged

You pay the rate in effect when you buy a Capacity Block, even if the block starts after a price change. The reservation fee is paid up front. Operating system fees are extra and charged only while instances run: $0 for Linux, or $1.8432 per instance-hour for Red Hat Enterprise Linux on P6 and P5 instances. AWS says it updates these prices with supply and demand, and the page now gives January 2027 as the next scheduled update.

## What to do

If you book short GPU reservations on AWS, price the same block again: a two-day block of one p6-b300.48xlarge now costs about $6,200 before OS fees. Compare that with On-Demand or a Savings Plan for the same instance, which this change did not touch.

results.title: 15 GPU list prices rose in September and none fell. Today AWS raises Capacity Blocks 15% — WPS
highlights:
# 15 GPU list prices rose in September and none fell. Today AWS raises Capacity Blocks 15%

FastGPU compared 176 posted on-demand GPU prices across September 2026: 15 rose, 0 fell. From October 7, AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML cost 15% more per GPU-hour, up to 26.5% outside the US.

 Dev.to · 2026-10-07 

 

In September 2026 we compared 176 posted on-demand GPU prices, each cloud's own published rate for each GPU it rents, between the first three and the last three days of the month. 15 ended the month higher, none ended it lower, and the other 161 did not move.

Today, October 7, AWS adds an increase of its own to EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML.

Everything below comes from the daily prices FastGPU records across GPU clouds, published as an open dataset, and from AWS's own pricing page. Every figure links to the page it comes from.

## 15 increases, no cuts 

All 15 came from two providers: Verda (10) and RunPod (5). Marketplaces, where each host sets its own price, are not part of this count.

## The typical price rose less 

The median of each provider's lowest posted on-demand price, counting only the providers that posted a price on all six of those days, so a provider joining or leaving never reads as a price move:

## The cheapest offer moves both ways 

The floor, the lowest posted on-demand price outside the hyperscalers (geometric mean of the first three days against the last three), is set by one or two providers at a time, so it swings:

- H100 SXM: $1.34 to $1.57 (+17.4%, set by 2 providers)
- H200: $2.60 to $2.16 (-17.1%, set by 2 providers)
- B200: $3.69 to $3.69 (0.0%, set by 1 provider)
- A100 80GB: $0.64 to $0.53 (-16.7%, set by 1 provider)

So the list prices at the larger GPU clouds drifted up while the cheapest deal stayed a moving target. For a job of a few hours, the floor is what you pay; for a quarter's budget, the list-price trend matters more.

...

On September 30 a V100 cost from $0.07/hr at Vast.ai to $2.95/hr at Oracle Cloud across 8 providers: $2.95 / $0.067 (the low before rounding) = 44.0x. It was the widest spread of the month: the same card, 8 sellers.

## AWS Capacity Blocks: 15% more from today, up to 26.5% outside the US 

AWS's Capacity Blocks pricing page says:

> Effective October 7, 2026, hourly rates per accelerator across all available AWS Regions will be: P6-B300 at $16.146 ($16.819 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P6-B200 at $14.208 ($14.801 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P5en at $7.895, P5e at $6.866, P5 at $5.970, P4de at $2.546, and P4d at $1.696.

Against the rates AWS published before, as recorded in our price-change log, per GPU per hour:

AWS now charges one rate in every Region, so blocks that used to be cheaper outside the US (P5 and P5en) rise the most. AWS publishes these rates to a tenth of a cent; our log shows them rounded to the cent. AWS also says Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand, and: "All other EC2 Capacity Block prices, as well as prices on fixed pricing models like On-Demand and Savings Plans, remain unchanged."

## What it means if you rent 

- A Capacity Block is reserved capacity: you book a start date and a length, and AWS guarantees the GPUs for it. That is a different product from an on-demand GPU you can stop at any time. Still, for scale: the cheapest posted H100 SXM is $1.79/hr at Vast.ai as of 2026-10-07 01:46 UTC, the September-end median across 16 providers was $3.70/hr, and a P5 Capacity Block is now $5.970/hr.
- If you were planning a reserved block, re-run the numbers: the reserve-or-rent calculator has the October 7 rates, and the GPU cluster page prices N GPUs for M months across providers' published term rates.
- List prices change without notice. A price alert emails you when a GPU drops below a price you choose, with no account.

## Data and method 

Posted prices, not transactions. The September report is computed from the recorded daily prices once the month is over and then frozen; every dated change is in the price-change log, also as JSON at `https://fastgpu.co/api/v1/price-changes`. The daily series is an open dataset (CC BY 4.0). Live prices in this post are as of 2026-10-07 01:46 UTC; the linked pages show the current ones. Some provider links on FastGPU are affiliate links; tables and every "cheapest" figure are ordered strictly by price.

results.title: GPU Pricing Forecast for AI Use - Sesame Disk
highlights:
- Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates 17-21% on October 1, 2026: H100 to $4.50/hr, H200 to $5.40, B200 to $8.50, B300 to $9.50.
- CoreWeave (CRWV) has pushed through roughly 37.5% in cumulative price increases since July, and is signing short contracts near $40 million per megawatt.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block reservation prices about 20% on July 1, 2026, with P6-B300 at $14.04 per accelerator-hour.
- Runpod’s fleet data shows B200 list prices up 31% between January and August 2026, with high-bandwidth memory effectively sold out into 2027.
- Custom ASIC shipments are growing 44.6% in 2026 versus 16.1% for merchant GPUs, per TrendForce.

## The Price Reversal: H100 Is No Longer Cheap

The clearest evidence comes from providers themselves. Nebius disclosed its October 1 card through customer communications reshared on Reddit and X. H100 hourly rates rose about 17% to $4.50, H200 rose 20% to $5.40, B200 nearly 19% to $8.50, and B300 about 21% to $9.50 from $7.85. CPU pricing moved too, with AMD (AMD) EPYC Genoa climbing 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour and Genoa memory up roughly 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour. NBIS shares jumped 9.15% premarket on September 17 when the hike surfaced, and the stock is up about 110% over six months, per GuruFocus.

...

The reversal is not limited to one neocloud. SemiAnalysis tracked Nvidia (NVDA) H100 one-year rental contracts climbing nearly 40% to $2.35 per GPU-hour in March 2026 from a $1.70 low in October 2025, as covered in this site’s August GPU price trends analysis. Runpod’s Fall 2026 State of AI Compute report, drawing on over 1.2 million users across 186 countries, found flagship GPU list prices rising through 2026, including a 31% B200 increase between January and August. The report’s framing is blunt: “Hardware is scarce, flagship GPU prices are rising, and AI bills are becoming material enough that teams can no longer treat the largest frontier model as the default answer to every problem,” according to the press release.

## Hyperscalers Are Raising Prices Too

The neocloud hikes might be dismissed as a small-provider phenomenon, but AWS’s July 1 change confirms the trend at the top of the market. Amazon Web Services (AMZN) raised EC2 Capacity Block reservation prices for machine-learning GPU instances by about 20%, citing “supply and demand dynamics.” New per-accelerator hourly rates span the fleet: P6-B300 at $14.04, P6-B200 at $12.355, P5 in US regions at $5.191, P5e at $5.97, and P4de at $2.214, per Investing.com.

Capacity Blocks are a reservation product, so the hike is structurally significant. Customers pay a premium over spot specifically to guarantee availability for time-bound training runs, so a 20% step-up signals that even committed capacity is scarce. AWS revenue grew 28% year over year to $37.6 billion in Q1 2026, its fastest cloud growth in more than three years, and Amazon has committed roughly $200 billion in 2026 capex. Reuters reported in March that Amazon is set to receive 1 million Nvidia GPUs by end-2027, itself a measure of how supply-constrained the high-end market remains.

...

The spread within a single card class is the real story: the same H100 a neocloud rents for $4.50 an hour costs AWS customers $5.19 to $6.87 on a reserved P5 instance, and the gap between neocloud and hyperscaler on identical silicon has run from 40% to 85% depending on card and term.

The calculation still comes down to use and throughput, but the spread between the two paths has widened in favor of whoever can keep hardware busy.

results.title: H100 Pricing History, in depth: reading tiered price data, normalising quotes, cost per useful hour and per token, and pricing a contract — Belgavi.AI Lab
highlights:
## The data: one index, three tiers

Silicon Data publishes an H100 rental index (ticker SDH100RT) and a blog post summarising it by period and by seller type. The medians below are per GPU-hour as that post reports them; they are one vendor's aggregation, not a market-wide truth, but they are dated and tiered, which is what you need.

| Period | Hyperscaler | Neocloud | Marketplace |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aug to Dec 2023 | $7.76 median | not in index | not in index |
| Jan to May 2024 | $7.92 median | not in index | not in index |
| Jun to Dec 2024 | $9.34 median | $2.99 median (from Jul) | $2.58 median (from Jun) |
| Jan to May 2025 | $8.96 median | $3.50 median | $2.29 median |
| Jun 2025 | $6.94 | $3.29 | $2.00 |
| Jul to Dec 2025 | $6.26 median | $3.33 median | $1.95 median |

Two other dated anchors come straight from providers. AWS announced price cuts of up to 45% for P5 (H100) On-Demand instances, effective 1 June 2025, consistent with the June 2025 step in the table (the index tier blends several hyperscalers, so it fell by less). And price moves are not one-way: in January 2026 AWS raised Capacity Block prices for its eight-GPU H200 instances (p5e.48xlarge and p5en.48xlarge) by about 15%, with steeper rises in some regions, as reported by DCD and The Register. Purchase prices for H100 boards and HGX systems were widely reported in the tens of thousands of dollars per GPU but were never published as list prices, so treat any single figure as anecdotal.

...

Second, hyperscaler and neocloud prices barely moved together. Hyperscaler list prices are sticky and set by price-book decisions; neocloud and marketplace prices react to supply. The hyperscaler premium buys things a bare GPU does not: integration with the provider's storage, identity and networking, the ability to start and stop instances by the hour, enterprise support and contracts your procurement team already has. Most large customers also never pay list; savings plans and private pricing apply.

...

The price you pay per GPU-hour is not your cost per unit of work. Three ratios sit between them. Utilisation is the fraction of paid hours the job is actually running (queueing, debugging, idle reservations). Failure loss is the fraction of running time thrown away by crashes and restarts since the last checkpoint. MFU is how much of the GPU's peak arithmetic the job uses while running. The script below turns a quote into dollars per useful hour and per million training tokens.

...

Key takeaway: Read H100 prices per tier: in one published index the hyperscaler median fell from about $9.34 per GPU-hour in late 2024 to $6.26 in late 2025, stepping down in June 2025; neocloud prices stayed roughly flat at $3 to $3.50; marketplace prices drifted from $2.58 to $1.95. Most disagreement in quoted prices is tier, unit and commitment mismatch. Normalise quotes, divide by utilisation, failure loss and MFU, compare on cost per token, and price contracts against both market decline and cost of delay.

results.title: GPU Rental Prices Fall 11% in September Despite Median ...
highlights:
# GPU Rental Prices Fall 11% in September Despite Median Price Holding Steady

The median price of an H100 GPU-hour fell 11% in September. Prices didn't. Our weekly median of listed on-demand H100 SXM rates went from $3.92 (week of Sep 7) to $3.49 (week of Sep 28). A headline writes itself: GPU rental prices are falling. Except they weren't. Over the same weeks our like-for-like index, which compares each cloud only with its own earlier price, ended the month at 100.8: up 0.8%, not down. What moved the median was the panel. We read 18 providers' H100 rates in the first week and 29 in the last, and the clouds that joined list below the ones already there. A median over a growing panel falls when cheaper sellers arrive, even if nobody cuts a price. Two more figures from the month: - monthly average: $3.88 per H100 GPU-hour, over 589 hourly readings - the four hyperscalers held at $9.90 all month; specialist GPU clouds ended at $3.20, 3.1 times less If you quote GPU prices, quote the index and the panel size with the median. Every figure links to the provider page it was read from, the weekly receipts list every quote, and the data is free under CC BY 4.0. September report (2 pages, PDF) and the frozen month: https://lnkd.in/eXe8EYxd #GPU #AIInfrastructure #CloudComputing #H100 #ComputePrices

results.title: GPU Rental Pricing: Hourly Rates and Total Cost — SiliconTicker
highlights:
## How much does it cost to rent a GPU?

A GPU rental price pays for access to a configured cloud machine for a period of time. The useful comparison is the cost of completing your workload, including the whole plan, runtime and additional fees. Chip model alone does not identify an equivalent service.

SiliconTicker compares public listings in USD per GPU-hour and retains the original plan price. A lower per-GPU rate can still require a more expensive multi-GPU plan. Prices are advertised observations; they do not confirm available capacity or a negotiated quote.

## Observed public GPU rental rates

These ranges cover the standard public-list and on-demand offers in our comparison catalog. Spot offers are excluded. Each row shows its underlying observation dates and sample size; this is a covered sample, not the entire rental market.

Standard offers · USD per GPU-hour · retrieved 2026-11-14

| GPU | Advertised range | Coverage | Observed / status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 4000 Ada | $0.76–$0.76 | 1 offer / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| RTX 6000 Ada | $1.57–$1.57 | 1 offer / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| L40S | $1.57–$1.67 | 2 offers / 2 providers | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| MI300X | $2.59–$2.59 | 2 offers / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| H100 | $3.37–$4.41 | 4 offers / 3 providers | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| MI325X | $3.80–$3.80 | 2 offers / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| H200 | $4.47–$4.47 | 2 offers / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $6.00–$8.25 | 4 offers / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |
| B300 | $16.00–$16.00 | 1 offer / 1 provider | 2026-11-14 · fresh |

Data: GPU Cloud Compare, CC-BY-4.0, normalized under our methodology. View exact plans, locations and upstream provider links in the GPU comparison. Read structured rows at /api/compare.

## Calculate the whole-plan cost

Compute cost = number of rented plans × plan price per hour × billed hours. The number of plans is your requested GPU count divided by GPUs per plan, rounded up. Keep the per-GPU unit separate from the billable plan unit.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE · NOT A CURRENT QUOTE

Suppose a four-GPU plan costs $12 per hour. Its normalized rate is $3 per GPU-hour. A job needing five GPUs requires two plans: eight billed GPUs, $24 per hour and $240 for ten hours. Multiplying five by $3 would understate the bill.

Add storage, data transfer, software, support and taxes where applicable. Include idle allocation and restart time. Check the provider’s minimum billing interval and whether a stopped machine remains billable. For example, DigitalOcean documents that GPU Droplet billing continues while powered off and ends when the Droplet is destroyed. DigitalOcean billing details.

...

A reserved block has different billing terms from an hourly rental. AWS charges the EC2 Capacity Block reservation price upfront and fixes it after reservation. Operating-system charges can apply separately while instances run; Savings Plans and Reserved Instance discounts do not apply to Capacity Blocks. AWS pricing and billing documentation.

...

- Hardware: exact GPU variant, memory per GPU, dedicated versus shared access and interconnect.
- Plan: GPU count, CPU, RAM, storage and network capacity. A plan total is not a single-GPU quote.
- Location: region, data residency, transfer cost and distance to your data.
- Terms: interruption, commitment length, minimum spend, support and capacity confirmation.
- Performance: measure runtime or throughput with your model, precision, batch size and software stack.

A GPU that costs twice as much per hour must complete comparable useful work more than twice as fast to lower compute cost, before other costs. Compare H100 and A100 by cost per result and consider interruption risk for Spot offers.

...

### Is the cheapest listing the cheapest workload?

Only if it can run the same workload with comparable output quality, runtime and service requirements. A smaller memory allocation, slower storage or extra restarts can erase a lower hourly rate.

### Does a listed price guarantee a GPU is available?

No. Confirm region, quota, delivery time and allocation with the provider. SiliconTicker marks comparison availability as unconfirmed.
